findings: State machine is per logical sample key (question_id, sample_slot), not per batch and not per raw completion. Canonical states: pending, in_flight, valid, repair_needed, retry_queued, superseded, exhausted, cancelled. Terminal states are valid, exhausted, cancelled. repair_needed is transient and must resolve in the same tick to retry_queued or exhausted.

A sample_slot is an intended vote index in 1..repeat_count. Repair never allocates a new slot. The failed attempt is marked superseded, linked via supersedes_attempt_id/superseded_by_attempt_id, and excluded from aggregation. The replacement attempt reuses the same sample_slot. This is replace-not-add and is the invariant that lets repair coexist with repeat_count and future confidence-triggered retries.

Independence rule: a malformed or unsupported quote, or a schema failure, retries only the affected question leaf. Valid sibling leaves in the same batch commit immediately, keep their batch_id/position provenance, and are never discarded, reparsed, or requeued. A batch is a transport envelope, not a scoring unit.

Validation gates, in order: (1) JSON/schema conformance against the rubric response contract, (2) per-question required fields and enum/range checks, (3) exact-quote structural checks (non-empty, bounded length, no ellipsis splicing unless the rubric allows it), (4) unsupported-quote check against the source text with normalized exact match. Failure at any gate is repair_needed for that leaf only.

Retry budget is bounded and hierarchical: max_attempts_per_slot (default 3 total = 1 initial + 2 repairs), max_repairs_per_question across all slots, max_repair_batches_per_job, and a wall-clock/job token budget. Quote failures and schema failures share the same attempt counter so a leaf cannot ping-pong forever by alternating failure classes. Exhaustion writes a terminal exhausted leaf and stops retry for that slot.

Batching remix rules: extract failed leaves; pack them into a new batch_id with still-pending leaves if needed, or a singleton if they are the remainder; never mix committed-valid leaves back in; preserve prompt_id and model_id unless an explicit escalation policy is set; cap remix batch size at the original batch cap; allow a failed leaf to land in a different batch and a different position. Remix is permitted because questions are independent; correlated batch-context bias is a reason to remix, not a reason to replay valid siblings.

Stop is cooperative and idempotent. On stop: do not launch retry_queued leaves; in_flight batches either complete parse-and-commit for already-returned tokens or cancel with no commit of ambiguous output; already-valid siblings stay valid; pending/retry_queued become cancelled; exhausted stays exhausted. A second stop is a no-op. The job is clean when no leaf remains in_flight or repair_needed.

Score-card disclosure is mandatory and machine-readable: n_intended, n_valid, n_exhausted, n_cancelled, n_superseded_attempts, repair_count by failure_class (schema, malformed_quote, unsupported_quote), remix_events, stop_reason, and per-question completeness (valid_slots/repeat_count). Aggregated scores must be computed only over valid leaves. Partial questions are flagged, not silently imputed.
recommendations: Implement LogicalSample as the unit of record: {question_id, sample_slot, attempt_index, batch_id, position_in_batch, prompt_id, prompt_hash, model_id, raw_response_id, parse_status, quote_check_status, failure_class, supersedes_attempt_id, superseded_by_attempt_id, status}. Persist every attempt, including superseded ones, for audit; aggregate only status=valid.

Use a single replace operator: commit_replacement(slot, new_attempt) that atomically marks the prior in-slot attempt superseded and installs the new attempt. Never append. Future confidence-triggered retries must call the same operator, or else explicitly allocate a new sample_slot with reason=confidence_retry so N changes are visible on the score card.

Repair prompt for an affected question should be isolated: include the question, the validator error, and optionally the rejected quote span, but not sibling questions' answers. Do not ask the model to repair the whole batch blob. If the original batch response is needed for provenance, store it on the superseded attempt only.

Exact-quote policy: require a verbatim contiguous source span after Unicode normalization (NFC, collapse only trailing/leading whitespace, preserve internal whitespace). Reject reconstructed paraphrases, stitched excerpts, and quotes that fail substring search. Unsupported quotes are not schema-repaired into empty strings; they retry. If the rubric allows no-evidence, that must be an explicit null quote with a reason code, not a fabricated span.

Scheduler algorithm: (a) commit valid siblings from a finished batch, (b) increment attempt_index on failed leaves and enqueue retry_queued if under budget else exhausted, (c) form the next batch by packing retry_queued first then pending, (d) emit a new batch_id, (e) exit when no pending/retry_queued remain or stop is set. Requeue into a different batch is the default after a failure, not a special case.

Hard limits to ship with: max_attempts_per_slot=3, max_repair_batches_per_job=2x ceil(n_leaves/batch_size), reject empty quotes and quotes longer than the source window, and fail-closed on validator exceptions (treat as schema failure, consume an attempt). Do not infinite-loop on a batch whose every leaf is exhausted.

Score-card consumer contract: if valid_slots < repeat_count for any question, mark that question incomplete and either omit it from consensus or report a lower-n score with an explicit n. Disclose repair so reviewers can distinguish a first-pass quote from a replaced quote. Never hide superseded attempts; never let them vote.

Clean-stop checklist: drain or cancel in_flight, freeze enqueue, write terminal statuses, emit score card with stop_reason in {completed, exhausted_budget, cancelled}, and make the snapshot idempotent so a crash-resume cannot double-count a replacement.
risks: If repair appends a new completion instead of replacing the sample_slot, repeat_count and confidence retries will silently inflate N and bias the rubric toward repaired outputs.
Replaying a whole batch because one quote failed discards valid sibling leaves, wastes budget, and can change already-accepted scores.
Unbounded quote/schema repair, or separate counters per failure class, can livelock a job that oscillates between invalid JSON and unsupported quotes.
Remixing failed questions into a new batch without a new batch_id, or mutating prompt_id/model_id implicitly, breaks provenance and makes score-card audit impossible.

Exact-match quote checks that are too strict (whitespace, curly quotes, hyphenation) will over-trigger repair; checks that are too loose will accept unsupported evidence. Either failure poisons the rubric.
Committing a partial parse from a cancelled in_flight batch can duplicate a leaf after resume. Stop must not commit ambiguous output.
Future confidence-triggered retries that add votes without disclosure will collide with this design unless they share the replace-or-explicit-new-slot rule.

Packing many independently failed questions into one repair batch can create a new correlated failure mode; singleton fallback must remain available when a remixed repair batch fails schema as a whole.
Score cards that report only the final number hide incompleteness: exhausted slots look like low variance instead of missing evidence.
output.summary: Repair is a bounded, per-leaf replacement of the intended sample slot: malformed or unsupported quotes and schema failures retry only the affected question, may remix into a new batch, never add a vote, never drop valid siblings, and stop cleanly under shared attempt budgets. repeat_count remains the intended N; retries and future confidence repeats must reuse the same replace-or-explicit-slot operator and disclose completeness, repair class, remix, and provenance on the score card.
